web_evidence.title: The Maidens
web_evidence.note: The publisher's authorized opening narrates Mariana externally as she across sustained prose, establishing the opening's third-person strand; it also identifies the apparent first-person grief line as a C. S. Lewis epigraph.

web_evidence.title: The Maidens Summary and Study Guide
web_evidence.note: Whole-book structural overview says the main narrative is third person from Mariana's perspective and that first-person narratives from Sebastian are interspersed through the six-part novel.

web_evidence.title: The Maidens Important Quotes
web_evidence.note: Book-wide textual analysis identifies Part 1, Chapter 7 as a first-person Sebastian letter chapter interrupting the otherwise third-person limited narrative, while quoting third-person passages from the opening through the epilogue.

web_evidence.title: The Maidens Prologue–Part 1, Chapter 10 Summary & Analysis
web_evidence.note: Section analysis records a shift to first person in Part 1, Chapter 7 and a return to Mariana's third-person limited perspective in Chapter 8, demonstrating alternation within Part 1.

web_evidence.title: The Maidens Part 4, Chapters 1–11 Summary & Analysis
web_evidence.note: Part 4 analysis identifies first-person narration in Chapters 1 and 11 surrounding sustained chapters externally following Mariana, showing that the first-person strand recurs well into the interior.

web_evidence.title: Alex Michaelides Writing Styles in The Maidens
web_evidence.note: The point-of-view discussion explicitly identifies third-person limited narration through Mariana. It describes the dominant strand but omits the recurring Sebastian interludes documented by the structural sources.

person_note: The novel alternates a dominant third-person limited narrative centered on Mariana with recurring, chapter-length first-person narratives by Sebastian that are ultimately understood as portions of his letter to Zoe. The quote set independently contains extensive third-person Mariana narration and repeated autobiographical I-passages matching that first-person strand. Those passages are therefore constitutive recurring sections, not isolated dialogue or incidental documents. q06434 is an upstream bucket anomaly: the authorized publisher excerpt shows that it is an attributed C. S. Lewis epigraph, so it is non-base. BookRags' third-person-only description captures the dominant Mariana strand but omits the interludes; the whole-book and part-level structural analyses resolve that omission. No material uncertainty remains about the sustained alternation.
